title: Handwritten things I wish I documented
content:
Purpose: brain dump of small practices, decisions, and micro-actions I keep forgetting to record. Wanted so I can point to something in 1:1s, or use as prompts during calibration. Not polished — raw handwriting-to-text style.

Top-of-mind things I keep forgetting
- When I take an ask off someone's plate, note the reason and expected follow-up date. I tend to close the loop externally but forget to write why I did it (tradeoff context).
- A/B of two ways I framed manager feedback last month: one was too tactical, the other landed as a behavior story. Save the behavioral one as template.
- Quick checklist for promo evidence: 1) 2 cross-team anecdotes, 2) 1 measurable outcome, 3) 1 scalability example (how the work made others faster).

Micro rituals I want to try (1–6 week tests)
- 5-minute morning capture: open doc, write 3 things I noticed yesterday that felt different. No judgement.
- End-of-week 10-minute triage: for each direct report, jot 1 risk, 1 win, 1 ask. Store under that person's heading in this doc.
- Weekly "question bank": keep a list of curious follow-ups from interviews/1:1s. Before promo calibrations, scan the bank for patterns.

Concrete entries to save for manager discussions
- Case: decided to centralize interview rubrics for product roles. Rationale: variability in candidate experience and inconsistent scoring. Outcome so far: reduced rework in scheduling (smaller win), still need to measure hire-to-offer delta. Next step: ask analytics to add a tag to candidate pipeline for centralized vs decentralized process.
- Case: declined a shadow interview pilot because capacity was low. Note to self: say explicitly "declining now to pilot at scale later" instead of vague "not ready".

Quick templates (short snippets to paste into messages)
- "Recap from our chat: you asked X, I committed to Y by DATE. If priorities shift, tell me and I'll reprioritize."
- "For calibration: here's 2-sentence impact, 1 quantitative signal, and 1 behavior example."

Metrics I check casually (not official dashboards)
- Time to close comms on people escalations (goal: <48h for triage note).
- % of hires with calibrated interviewer feedback within 72 hours (goal: 85%).
- Number of policy exceptions granted per month (visible trend = risk).

Tiny decisions I want to document when they happen
- When I let someone skip a rotation for parental reasons: note length, how role coverage works, and expectations on ramp-back.
- When I grant a one-off comp exception: write short justification and at least one plan to avoid repetition.

Unresolved questions
- Should we make manager calibration a monthly short-form (10m per manager) or keep quarterly longer sessions? Tradeoffs: monthly better signal, more time burden. Pilot idea: pick one pod and run monthly micro-calibration for 3 months.
- How to capture soft-skill progress without creating onerous paperwork? Maybe 1–2 sentence narratives attached to cross-functional PRs?

Small experiments to run (hypotheses)
- Experiment A: share 1 anonymized success story weekly in #people-ops to normalize different career paths. Hypothesis: increases manager examples for calibration by 15% in 6 weeks.
- Experiment B: 10-minute "what went well" note after every onboarding cohort. Hypothesis: identifies 2 repeat friction points per cohort.

Prompts for 1:1s (to use a few of each time)
- What felt different about your work this week?
- What interaction made you more effective? Less effective?
- If you were me, what would you stop doing?

Archive notes (things to copy to other places when formalized)
- Interview rubric change rationale -> Confluence: hiring/process/rubrics (when we have numbers).
- Shadow interview playbook -> internal repo: people-ops/playbooks/shadow-interviews (once pilot succeeds).

Signals I want visible in my inbox (to stop re-asking)
- If someone reports a blocker that will cause a >1-week delay, they should CC me with a short "impact note".
- When a policy exception is requested, include role, duration, and mitigation plan in the request.

Notes to self (short, hand-writing-y)
- Stop apologizing for being decisive. Capture the tradeoffs instead.
- When I say "let me think and get back", do a 24h touchpoint even if no answer.
- Keep a folder of 3 anonymized stories per quarter for promotion calibration.

Next actions (this week)
- Try the 5-minute morning capture for 5 weekdays and note the difference.
- Add tag to the hiring sheet to measure centralized rubric trial (ask analytics).
- Draft a 1-paragraph template for policy-exception notes and share with Marcus.

Reference snippets (copy-paste friendly)
- "Impact: consolidated rubric reduced scheduling churn and improved interviewer calibration; signal: variance in scores dropped 22% across two roles; behavior: initiated cross-functional interviewer training."
- "Policy exception note: role, reason, duration, mitigation, owner-of-followup."

End note: keep this messy. The point of this doc is fast capture, not polish. If something looks like it will be useful to others, move it out with a date and a one-line summary.
